I give up.

The file is unchanged and still contains the `sorry`. Mathlib (the compiled copy I searched) has no counting result for labelled trees or rooted forests, so there is nothing to reuse for the count.

The math is sound: the condition is equivalent to every cycle of the functional graph meeting {1..k}. Cutting the out-edge of each element of {1..k} turns f into a rooted forest on [n] with root set {1..k}, plus an arbitrary target in [n] for each root. That gives k·n^(n-k-1)·n^k = k·n^(n-1). The bijection is clear on paper, but formalizing it in Lean requires proving the forest count k·n^(n-k-1) from scratch, which is a large development I did not attempt.
